sources.title: Hepatotoxicity of high affinity gapmer antisense oligonucleotides is mediated by RNase H1 dependent promiscuous reduction of very long pre-mRNA transcripts
sources.claim: RNase H1 depletion attenuated off-target transcript reduction and liver injury for tested high-affinity gapmers, providing a sequence-dependent hybridization alternative to a purely protein-binding explanation.
sources.locator: Results: Hepatotoxicity of LNA ASOs is RNase H1 dependent; Figure 5A–B. Figure 1A and Results first subsection for tolerated controls.
sources.context: Balb/c mice; 13 3–10–3 LNA gapmers in initial single-dose study; mechanistic challenge at 25 or 75 mg/kg after anti-RNase H1 MOE pretreatment; liver RNA and plasma ALT.

counterevidence.evidence: Six of 13 initial LNA gapmers were tolerated up to 300 mg/kg within 96 h; Figure 1A. Later cEt controls also tolerated, Supplementary Figure S7.

sources.limitations: Neither the HeLa case nor a proof of its mechanism; sequence, exposure and assay differ. RNase H1-associated effects do not uniquely distinguish all downstream toxicity pathways.
sources.falsification_experiment: For the case pair, compare transcript perturbations and caspase response after controlled RNase H1 reduction alongside protein-binding measurements.
sources.suggested_placement: Introduction sequence×chemistry rationale; HeLa mechanism alternatives; Discussion against universal LNA rules.

sources.title: In silico and in vitro evaluation of exonic and intronic off-target effects form a critical element of therapeutic ASO gapmer optimization
sources.claim: BACH1-directed ASOs reduced experimentally tested exonic and intronic off-target RNAs; motif descriptors alone therefore cannot identify a specific off-target transcript.
sources.locator: Figures 1–2 (RNA/protein validation); Figure 3 (26 tested candidate off-targets for GSK2910546A); Figure 4 (duplex stability comparison).
sources.context: Human NHBE cells with gymnotic uptake and A549 lipid transfection; Figure 1 NHBE concentration 0.1–5 µM; Figure 2D protein measurements after 20 µM for 48 h.

counterevidence.target_claim: Any sequence-similar transcript is a functional off-target
counterevidence.evidence: Experimentally tested off-targets differed in potency, Figure 3; candidate matches require measurement.

sources.limitations: Molecular off-target activity, not direct validation of manuscript toxicity predictions. Cell type and delivery affect relevance; no exact case-sequence match established.
sources.falsification_experiment: Measure candidate transcript and protein changes for matched chemistry variants, rather than infer target engagement from a short motif.
sources.suggested_placement: Descriptor rationale and HeLa alternate explanation.

sources.title: Antisense oligonucleotides containing locked nucleic acid improve potency but cause significant hepatotoxicity in animals
sources.claim: Matched LNA/MOE series demonstrated that increased target potency can coexist with worse liver tolerability; molecular improvement is endpoint-specific rather than a single universal direction.
sources.locator: Figures 3–4 (TRADD reduction and transaminases); Figure 5 (histopathology and injury markers); Figures 7–8 (ApoB and PTEN series).
sources.context: Mouse liver; gapmers with LNA or MOE wings and DNA gaps. Figure 5 reports 4.5 µmol/kg twice weekly for three weeks.

counterevidence.target_claim: Every LNA substitution improves potency or inevitably increases toxicity
counterevidence.evidence: The study reports variable potency effects; Burel2016 provides tolerated LNA controls. Do not extrapolate its selected series to the entire chemistry class.

sources.limitations: Not the 13-mer HeLa case or a position-12 intervention. Target, sequence, gap architecture and exposure differ; toxicity mechanism is not resolved by chemistry comparison alone.
sources.falsification_experiment: Measure both target knockdown and caspase response for the proposed position-swap series to distinguish potency from tolerability.
sources.suggested_placement: Introduction chemical design trade-offs; HeLa discussion.

sources.title: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides can displace NEAT1 RNA and form nuclear paraspeckle-like structures
sources.claim: Both sugar chemistry and PS content affected binding of tested nuclear proteins, supporting interpretation of mixed sequence–sugar–backbone descriptors rather than isolated chemistry labels.
sources.locator: Figure 1D (same-sequence 2′ modifications), 1E–F (PS number and length); Figure 6G (RNase H1-independent NEAT1 reduction).
sources.context: Affinity-selection experiments with 5–10–5 cEt capture ASO; HeLa and other cell systems; Figure 6H uses 50 nM overnight transfection.

counterevidence.target_claim: Every ASO-associated RNA reduction is canonical target-directed RNase H1 cleavage
counterevidence.evidence: Control-ASO NEAT1 reduction was not prevented by RNase H1 depletion, Figure 6G.

sources.limitations: Binding/relocalization and NEAT1 findings are not a toxicity assay or direct evidence for the case pair. A binding threshold for one protein is not a universal PS design rule.
sources.falsification_experiment: Compare case variants by protein pull-down and subcellular localization at matched concentration, with uptake controls.

sources.title: Identification and characterization of intracellular proteins that bind oligonucleotides with phosphorothioate linkages
sources.claim: Intracellular ASO-binding proteins can either facilitate or inhibit antisense activity, so protein binding cannot be assigned one uniform beneficial or harmful meaning.
sources.locator: Figure 2 (La/NPM1 depletion), Figure 5 (Ku70/Ku80 depletion), Figure 6 (competition with RNase H1), Figure 7 (nuclear accumulation).
sources.context: HeLa protein perturbation and target-RNA assays; Figure 7 uses 50 nM fluorescent ASO for five hours; distinct free-uptake localization experiments use 2 µM for 24 h.

counterevidence.target_claim: More intracellular protein binding always implies greater toxicity
counterevidence.evidence: Opposing effects of different proteins on ASO activity; experiments measure activity/localization, not a universal toxicity relationship.

sources.limitations: Not direct toxicity or same-case evidence. Fluorescent localization and transfection conditions cannot supply a HeLa caspase effect size.
sources.falsification_experiment: Measure localization, target reduction and caspase response separately when testing the chemistry pair.
sources.suggested_placement: Discussion: alternative explanations for chemistry-associated model dependence.

excluded.reason: Relevant metadata verified but full-text XML returned empty; no figure-level claim promoted in this review.

unresolved: No new exact-sequence experimental evidence for the V11 HeLa case was found. These original studies enrich mechanism alternatives, not measured labels or causal attribution. No new external validation cohort was assembled.
